title: Setting Up Atlas and mongosh
summary: Create a free MongoDB Atlas cluster, install mongosh, connect with a connection string and run your first shell commands, or run MongoDB 8 locally instead.
introduction: Before you can store a document you need a server to talk to and a shell to talk with. MongoDB Atlas gives you a free hosted cluster in a few minutes, and mongosh is the official shell for sending commands to it. This lesson walks through creating the cluster, adding a database user and a network rule, installing mongosh, connecting, and the handful of shell commands you will use in every session. It also shows how to run MongoDB 8 locally if you prefer to work offline.
learningObjectives: Create a free Atlas cluster with a database user and an IP access rule
Install mongosh and connect to a cluster with a connection string
Switch databases, list collections and insert a first document from the shell

blocks.text: **MongoDB Atlas** is MongoDB's hosted service. Its free tier, an *M0* cluster, costs nothing, needs no credit card, gives you 512 MB of storage and runs a real three-member replica set, which matters later for transactions. A **local** installation of MongoDB Community Server is also free and works offline, but by default it runs as a single server. This tutorial uses Atlas; every command works the same against a local server, and the end of this lesson shows how to start one.

items: Sign up at [mongodb.com/atlas](https://www.mongodb.com/atlas) and create a project.
Choose to create a cluster, pick the free **M0** tier, a cloud provider and the region closest to you, and keep the default name `Cluster0`. Provisioning takes a few minutes.

Under **Security**, open **Database Access** and add a database user with a username and a strong password. Give it *Read and write to any database* for now; the [Security Basics](/tutorials/mongodb/security-basics) lesson narrows that down.
Open **Network Access** and add your current IP address. Atlas rejects every connection from an address that is not on this list.
Back on the cluster, click **Connect**, choose the **Shell** option and copy the connection string.

blocks.text: A connection string looks like this:

The scheme `mongodb+srv://` means *DNS seed list*: Atlas publishes the addresses of the cluster's servers in DNS, so the string stays short and keeps working when servers are replaced. `appuser` is the database user, `<password>` is a placeholder for its password, and the host name identifies your cluster. Options such as `?retryWrites=true` may follow the slash.
mongosh is a separate download from the server. On Windows, download the installer from the MongoDB download centre and accept the defaults. On macOS and Linux a package manager is quicker:

blocks.code:
# macOS with Homebrew
brew tap mongodb/brew
brew install mongosh

# Ubuntu and Debian, after adding the MongoDB apt repository
sudo apt-get install -y mongodb-mongosh

# any platform: check the installation
mongosh --version

blocks.text: Pass the connection string without the credentials and give the username as an option, so that mongosh prompts for the password instead of leaving it in your shell history:

blocks.title: Output (abridged; versions vary)
blocks.content:
Enter password: ********
Current Mongosh Log ID: 69a3a9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8
Connecting to:    mongodb+srv://<credentials>@cluster0.ab12cd.mongodb.net/?appName=mongosh+2.5.6
Using MongoDB:    8.0.12
Using Mongosh:    2.5.6

Atlas atlas-ab12cd-shard-0 [primary] test>

blocks.text: The banner confirms the server version, and the prompt tells you three things: you are connected to an Atlas cluster, to its *primary* member (the one that accepts writes), and the current database is `test`. For a local server the prompt is simply `test>`.

mongosh is a JavaScript environment with a few shell-style helpers. `use` switches the current database, `db` refers to it, and `show collections` lists what it contains. Switching to a database that does not exist yet is fine: MongoDB creates the database and the collection the moment you insert the first document.
`show collections` printed nothing because `shop` is still empty. Insert one document and look again:

blocks.code:
db.products.insertOne({ name: 'Mechanical keyboard', price: 89.5 })
show collections

blocks.text: The result says the server acknowledged the write and shows the `_id` it stored; your `ObjectId` value will differ, because it is generated on the fly. The `products` collection now exists, and `show dbs` would list `shop` alongside the system databases `admin` and `local`.

rows: Lists the databases you can see, with their size on disk
Makes `shop` the current database (created on first insert)
Prints the name of the current database
Lists the collections in the current database
Lists the methods available on a collection

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text: If mongosh waits about thirty seconds and then fails with `MongoServerSelectionError`, the usual cause is that your current IP address is not on the Atlas access list, for example because you moved to another network. Add the new address under Network Access and connect again. The next most common cause is a password containing characters such as `@`, `:` or `/` pasted straight into the connection string; such characters must be percent-encoded, which is one more reason to let mongosh prompt for the password.

If you have Docker, one command starts a MongoDB 8 server on the default port 27017; without Docker, install MongoDB Community Server from the download centre and it runs as a background service on the same port. Connect to either with a plain `mongodb://` string:

blocks.title: Output (abridged; the container id is random)
blocks.content:
3f9c2a8e1b7d6c5a4e3f2d1c0b9a8f7e6d5c4b3a2f1e0d9c8b7a6f5e4d3c2b1a
Current Mongosh Log ID: 69a3a9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e9
Connecting to:    mongodb://localhost:27017/?directConnection=true&serverSelectionTimeoutMS=2000&appName=mongosh+2.5.6
Using MongoDB:    8.0.12
Using Mongosh:    2.5.6

test>

blocks.text: A local server started this way has no authentication and no replication, which is fine on your own machine for learning. Remember two consequences: anyone who can reach the port can read the data, so never expose it to the internet, and multi-document transactions will not work until the server is started as a replica set, as the [Transactions](/tutorials/mongodb/transactions) lesson explains.

questions.question: You run `use inventory` in mongosh and the database does not exist. What happens?
questions.explanation: `use` only changes the current database. MongoDB creates the database, and the collection, when the first document is inserted.
options: mongosh prints an error because the database does not exist
The database is created immediately with an empty default collection
The current database switches to `inventory`; it is created when you insert the first document
mongosh asks whether you want to create it

questions.question: Atlas accepts connections from any IP address as long as the username and password are correct.
questions.explanation: Atlas rejects connections from addresses that are not on the project's IP access list, regardless of credentials. Add your address under Network Access.
